title: Motorways & Smart Motorways
whatItIs: Fast roads with their own rules: who may use them, joining, lane discipline, red X closures, hard shoulders and emergency areas.

keyFacts.text: Provisional car licence holders MUST NOT use motorways unless with an ADI, in a dual-control car with red L/D plates.

keyFacts: Joining: give priority to traffic on the motorway and match your speed to the left lane.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT drive in a lane closed by a red X or red flashing lights.
You MUST NOT use a hard shoulder except in an emergency or when directed.

keyFacts: Keep in the left lane unless overtaking; overtake only on the right.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT reverse, cross the central reservation or drive against traffic, unless police or traffic officers direct.

items.title: Red X / red flashing lights
items.text: Lane closed: you MUST NOT drive in it. A speed limit or 'END' shows it has reopened.

items.title: Hard shoulder as a lane
items.text: Only when a speed limit shows above it. Red X or blank sign: emergencies only.

items.title: Emergency areas
items.text: Blue sign, orange SOS phone. Emergencies only; MUST phone before rejoining.

items.title: Right lane (3+ lanes)
items.text: MUST NOT be used by vehicles towing trailers or by larger goods and passenger vehicles.

onTheTest.question: Your learner wants motorway practice. What is required?
onTheTest.why: Rule 253: provisional car licence holders MUST NOT use motorways unless with an ADI, in a dual-controlled car with red L plates (D plates in Wales).

onTheTest.question: A red X shows above the left lane. What must your pupil do?
onTheTest.why: Rule 258: a red X marks a closed lane where people or stopped vehicles may be. You MUST follow the signs to move to an open lane and MUST NOT drive in the closed one.

traps: Missed your exit? Carry on to the next one: never reverse, even on a slip road.
After leaving, 50 mph can feel like 30 mph: check the speedometer.
Amber flashing lights: speed up only after a non-flashing signal or 'END'.
Smart motorways change limits and lane use: the national standard says obeying them is vital.
